wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/byref_slot_test.py: """The by-ref out-parameter test follows the refusal to where it now lives.

The checker no longer refuses `$would = "untouched"; flock($h, LOCK_SH, $would);` — the merge
widens the variable, as php does. The BACKEND still refuses, because the IR local keeps the type
its first assignment gave it: a by-reference write emits no store for the slot type to follow.

That is a refusal, not a corruption, and the distinction is the whole point of the guard this test
was written for — an int written into a string slot used to overwrite the pointer half and
segfault on the next read. MEASURED: `php -n`
